item.title: Forvia Hella wins orders for EnergyCore solutions from two automakers
item.description: Forvia Hella has received orders for its EnergyCore solutions from two automakers in America and Europe, with a combined worth of around €500 million ($560 million), Forvia said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Forvia Hella has received orders for its EnergyCore solutions from two automakers in America and Europe, with a combined worth of around €500 million ($560 million), Forvia (FRVIA.PA) said on Thursday. "The combined order volume from both customers is in the mid-three-digit million-euro range," the French auto parts maker said in a statement, which did not name the customers. ($1 = 0.8935 euros)

item.title: FORVIA HELLA décroche deux commandes majeures pour ses solutions EnergyCore
item.description: FORVIA a annoncé jeudi que sa filiale FORVIA HELLA avait remporté deux importantes commandes en série pour ses solutions EnergyCore pour un montant cumulé "dans la fourchette des centaines de millions d'euros".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: FORVIA (FRVIA.PA) a annoncé jeudi que sa filiale FORVIA HELLA avait remporté deux importantes commandes en série pour ses solutions EnergyCore pour un montant cumulé "dans la fourchette des centaines de millions d'euros". Les contrats portent sur un système de gestion de batterie haute tension "X-in-1", ainsi que sur un PowerPack 48 volts. Le groupe précise que le lancement de la production est prévu respectivement en décembre 2027 et au printemps 2028.

item.title: Deutschland und Großbritannien verstärken gemeinsame Sabotage-Abwehr

item.content:encoded: Großbritannien und Deutschland wollen am Donnerstag eine gemeinsame Partnerschaft zur Bekämpfung von Sabotage und Cyberangriffen ins Leben rufen. Nach Angaben der britischen Regierung geht es dabei um den Informationsaustausch und die Koordinierung im Kampf gegen Bedrohungen für die kritische Infrastrukturen. Die deutschen Geheimdienste hatten erst am Montag vor der wachsenden Gefahr hybrider Bedrohungen durch Russland gewarnt. Die Festnahme des früheren BND-Chefs August Hanning und ein mutmaßliches Datenleck ins Ausland über Jahre hatten zuletzt Zweifel geschürt, ob befreundete Dienste noch vorbehaltlos vertrauliche Informationen mit ihren deutschen Partnern teilen. Am Donnerstag kommt der britische Premierminister Andy Burnham zu seinem Antrittsbesuch nach Berlin und wird mit Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz das sogenannte Kensington-Abkommen besiegeln, das als deutsch-britischer Freundschaftsvertrag dienen soll. Ziel beider Regierungen ist es, das 2020 aus der EU ausgetretene Königreich wieder möglichst eng an die Union anzubinden. Burnham hatte zuletzt betont, dass auch ein Wiedereintritt seines Landes in die EU eine Option sei. In der EU wird allerdings darauf verwiesen, dass es dazu zunächst eine eindeutige Stimmungslage auf der Insel geben müsse. Derzeit befürwortet eine Mehrheit der Briten eine erneute EU-Mitgliedschaft.

item.title: South African rand steady ahead of manufacturing data, muted dollar offers support
item.description: The South African rand was steady in early trade on Thursday ahead of the release of domestic manufacturing data, supported by a muted dollar as investors assessed the likelihood of another US Federal Reserve interest rate hike this year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The South African rand was steady in early trade on Thursday ahead of the release of domestic manufacturing data, supported by a muted dollar as investors assessed the likelihood of another US Federal Reserve interest rate hike this year. At 0549 GMT, the rand traded at 16.64 against the dollar , a whisker away from its previous close of 16.63. South Africa's statistics agency will publish data on manufacturing output (ZAMAN=ECI) at 1100 GMT, with analysts polled by Reuters expecting a 0.6% year-on-year increase in August, from a 1.1% year-on-year rise in July. Nedbank economists expect manufacturing output to slip back into contraction after July's temporary rebound. The sector remains under pressure from high input and power costs, while US tariffs , fuel price hikes and supply shortages continue to weigh on production and competitiveness, Nedbank said. The greenback was steady against a basket of currencies, as traders assessed the likelihood of another Federal Reserve rate hike this year after [USN:L6N45U07E TEXT:"minutes"] from the September meeting revealed divisions among policymakers over the need for further tightening. In common with other risk-sensitive currencies, the rand often takes cues from global drivers such as US economic indicators and monetary policy, in addition to domestic economic data. South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond was also flat in early deals, with the yield at 8.835%.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Die Stimmung unter den Selbstständigen und Kleinstunternehmen in Deutschland hat sich im September das fünfte Mal in Folge aufgehellt. Das entsprechende Barometer für das Geschäftsklima stieg von minus 19,7 Zählern im August auf minus 18,8 Punkte, wie das Münchner Ifo-Institut am Donnerstag zu seiner Umfrage mitteilte. Vor allem die Erwartungen fielen weniger pessimistisch aus. Aber auch die laufenden Geschäfte wurden nicht mehr so kritisch bewertet. "Für Optimismus ist es noch zu früh, aber es gibt Anzeichen für eine allmähliche Erholung", sagte Ifo-Expertin Katrin Demmelhuber. "Bei den Selbstständigen zeigt sich bislang jedoch nur eine langsame Verbesserung." Die Unsicherheit bleibt sehr hoch: Fast vier von fünf Befragten fällt es schwer oder eher schwer, ihre zukünftige Geschäftsentwicklung einzuschätzen, fanden die Ifo-Forscher heraus. Damit bleibt die Planbarkeit für Soloselbstständige und Kleinstunternehmen stark eingeschränkt. Für kleine Betriebe wird es zudem zunehmend schwieriger, über Banken Zugang zu frischen Krediten zu erhalten. Im abgelaufenen dritten Quartal stieg der Anteil an Soloselbstständigen und Kleinstunternehmen mit Schwierigkeiten bei Kreditverhandlungen von 44,8 auf 54,4 Prozent. Zum Vergleich: In der Gesamtwirtschaft sank der Anteil dagegen von 40,1 auf 32,8 Prozent. Zugleich ließ die Kreditnachfrage der Selbstständigen nochmals nach: Nur noch 7,8 Prozent führten Gespräche mit Banken über Darlehen, nach 9,3 Prozent im Vorquartal. "Die Ergebnisse deuten darauf hin, dass sich der Zugang zu Bankkrediten für kleine Betriebe deutlich erschwert", sagte Demmelhuber. "Gleichzeitig fragen immer weniger Selbständige überhaupt Kredite bei Banken nach." Das Ifo-Institut befragt für den Indikator in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Softwareunternehmen Jimdo monatlich etwa 1800 Soloselbstständige sowie Kleinstunternehmen mit bis zu neun Mitarbeitenden. Der Verband der Gründer und Selbstständigen Deutschland (VGSD) sieht die Politik in der Pflicht, damit die allgemeine Konjunkturerholung auch bei den Mitgliedern ankommt. Eine potenzielle Wachstumsbremse sei die geplante Rentenpflicht für künftige Selbstständige, "die ohne gleichzeitige Reform der Beitragsbemessung zu einem massiven Einbruch des Gründungsgeschehens führen wird", sagte der Vorstandsvorsitzende des VGSD, Andreas Lutz.

item.title: Drones hit Yandex data centre in first major attack on Russian data hub
item.description: Drones hit a major data centre in Russia's Ryazan region owned by the country's leading AI and technology company Yandex , the company said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Drones hit a major data centre in Russia's Ryazan region owned by the country's leading AI and technology company Yandex , the company said on Thursday. It added that the attack caused a fire and forced the company to fully suspend the centre's operations. The company said it was dealing with the consequences and restoring affected services. The company said that its core consumer services were not affected. Yandex runs YandexGPT, one of Russia's leading generative AI models. The attack on the Yandex data centre followed a wave of Russian attacks on Ukrainian data centres in recent weeks. Previously there were no confirmed major Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian data centres. On the website of its Yandex Cloud service, the company said there were problems with the electricity supply at one data centre "zone", and recommended customers use other zones.

item.title: Allemagne-Baisse surprise des exportations en août
item.description: Les exportations allemandes ont baissé de façon inattendue en août, accusant un recul de 0,8% par rapport au mois précédent, selon les données de l'Office fédéral de la statistique publiées jeudi.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les exportations allemandes ont baissé de façon inattendue en août, accusant un recul de 0,8% par rapport au mois précédent, selon les données de l'Office fédéral de la statistique publiées jeudi. Les économistes interrogés par Reuters avaient tablé au contraire sur une hausse de +0,6% de ces exportations, après -0,8% en juillet. Les importations ont, quant à elles, augmenté de 0,9% sur un mois en août, après une baisse de -5,7% le mois précédent et contre un consensus à +2,6%.

item.title: Le bilan de la vaste attaque russe en Ukraine mercredi passe à 32 morts
item.description: Le bilan de la pluie de missiles et de drones russes qui s'est abattue sur l'Ukraine dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi est passé à 32 morts et 100 blessés après le décès de deux personnes tuées par des débris de drones mercredi soir dans une banlieue de Kyiv.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le bilan de la pluie de missiles et de drones russes qui s'est abattue sur l'Ukraine dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi est passé à 32 morts et 100 blessés après le décès de deux personnes tuées par des débris de drones mercredi soir dans une banlieue de Kyiv. Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky a qualifié cette attaque de l'une des plus [USN:L8N45T035 TEXT:""odieuses""] depuis le début de l'invasion à grande échelle de l'Ukraine par la Russie en février 2022. La frappe la plus meurtrière a eu lieu à Prylouky, dans l'oblast de Tchernihiv (nord), où un missile russe a anéanti le cinquième étage d'un immeuble résidentiel. Au moins 22 personnes dont cinq enfants, ont été tuées, selon les autorités locales qui ont également fait état d'une cinquantaine de blessés.

item.title: Los tránsitos por Ormuz caen a su mínimo en más de dos meses tras ataques, según datos
item.description: El número de buques que transitaban por el estrecho de Ormuz cayó hasta su nivel más bajo en más de dos meses después de que los ataques contra petroleros en esta importante vía marítima alcanzaran la semana pasada su nivel más alto desde el inicio de la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel con Irán, según los datos del sector naviero.
item.dc:creator: Florence Tan
item.content:encoded: El número de buques que transitaban por el estrecho de Ormuz cayó hasta su nivel más bajo en más de dos meses después de que los ataques contra petroleros en esta importante vía marítima alcanzaran la semana pasada su nivel más alto desde el inicio de la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel con Irán, según los datos del sector naviero. Siete buques de mercancías atravesaron el estrecho el martes, lo que supone la cifra más baja desde el 23 de julio, según datos de la empresa de análisis Kpler. "El crudo que cruzó el estrecho se redujo un 27% respecto al máximo registrado durante la guerra la semana anterior, hasta situarse en al menos 10,1 millones de barriles al día", escribieron los analistas de Kpler Emmanuel Belostrino y Yui Torikata en una nota del 6 de octubre. "Esto supone una vuelta a la media de septiembre, pero representa el 74% de su nivel anterior a la guerra". La mayor parte de la caída se produjo en las transferencias de buque a buque en el golfo de Omán, donde los cargamentos se transfieren entre petroleros, añadieron. Sin embargo, las exportaciones desde la costa del golfo de Omán y el mar Rojo aumentaron hasta los 6,7 millones de barriles al día, más del doble de los niveles previos a la guerra, según los analistas, lo que compensó la pérdida de suministro procedente de Ormuz. Esto contribuyó a mantener las exportaciones totales de crudo de Oriente Medio en el nivel anterior a la guerra, señalaron. El número de buques que transitaban por el estrecho subió ligeramente hasta los 10 el miércoles, pero quedó muy por debajo de la cifra diaria de más de 20 registrada el domingo y el lunes, según los datos. En los últimos dos días entraron en el estrecho más buques de los que salieron. Las cifras excluyen a los buques que cruzan con los transpondedores de su Sistema de Identificación Automática apagados para evitar ser detectados. Los datos de LSEG sobre todos los buques que cruzaron el estrecho indicaron ocho el martes, repartidos a partes iguales entre entradas y salidas, lo que supone un descenso respecto a los 14 del día anterior. Entre ellas se encontraban cinco petroleros y el buque cisterna de gas natural licuado Al Mafyar, que cargó en Ras Laffan (Qatar) y tenía previsto poner rumbo a Port Qasim (Pakistán), añadió LSEG. Los ataques contra petroleros que navegan por el estrecho de Ormuz alcanzaron la semana pasada su nivel más alto desde que comenzó la guerra en Irán, según fuentes de seguridad marítima que realizan un seguimiento de los incidentes, al tiempo que los productores del golfo Pérsico intensificaban sus exportaciones. En el más reciente incidente, unos proyectiles impactaron en un petrolero a 51 millas náuticas (94 kilómetros) al norte de Madinat ash Shamal, en Qatar, y se han registrado víctimas, informó el miércoles la agencia United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). Antes del inicio de la guerra en Irán, el 28 de febrero, atravesaban el estrecho cada día unos 125 grandes buques comerciales, entre los que se encontraban petroleros, gaseros, graneleros y portacontenedores. Sus cargamentos representaban una quinta parte del suministro mundial de petróleo crudo y gas natural licuado.

item.title: Washington y Moscú debaten posible inversión de EEUU en los gasoductos Nord Stream
item.description: Altos cargos rusos y estadounidenses, entre ellos el enviado especial de EEUU Jared Kushner, han mantenido conversaciones para incorporar a un inversor estadounidense a los gasoductos Nord Stream, que suministraban gas a Alemania antes de que Rusia invadiera Ucrania, según cinco personas con conocimiento de la situación.
item.dc:creator: John O'Donnell, Gram Slattery, David Gauthier-Villars
item.content:encoded: Altos cargos rusos y estadounidenses, entre ellos el enviado especial de EEUU Jared Kushner, han mantenido conversaciones para incorporar a un inversor estadounidense a los gasoductos Nord Stream, que suministraban gas a Alemania antes de que Rusia invadiera Ucrania, según cinco personas con conocimiento de la situación. En las conversaciones participaron Kirill Dmitriev, asesor cercano del presidente ruso Vladimir Putin, y Kushner, yerno del presidente estadounidense Donald Trump, según las fuentes. Kushner, que ha estado intentando mediar para lograr una tregua entre Rusia y Ucrania, considera que los negocios son fundamentales para restablecer la paz. Un acuerdo de este tipo permitiría a los inversores estadounidenses beneficiarse de los flujos de energía hacia Europa una vez que termine la guerra. Dmitriev y Kushner se han reunido en Moscú y Nueva York en las últimas semanas. Aunque no está claro hasta qué punto hablaron del Nord Stream en esas ocasiones, el tema sigue estando sobre la mesa, indicaron dos de las fuentes a Reuters. "Cualquier acuerdo deberá ser negociado por Rusia con la DFC (Corporación Financiera para el Desarrollo Internacional de EEUU) y el Tesoro, y debe beneficiar a los contribuyentes y a las empresas estadounidenses", dijo un representante de la Casa Blanca al ser preguntado sobre las conversaciones relativas al gasoducto. "No ha habido debates recientes sobre Nord Stream", dijo a Reuters. Dmitriev, que ha abogado por la reanudación de las ventas de gas ruso a Alemania, se reunió el mes pasado con representantes de los Departamentos de Energía y del Tesoro de EEUU para debatir posibles iniciativas energéticas entre EEUU y Rusia. Un representante de Dmitriev se negó a hacer comentarios. Sigue sin estar claro hasta qué punto Washington está interesado en impulsar la reanudación de los flujos de gas ruso hacia Alemania, que es el mayor consumidor de energía de Europa. Un responsable estadounidense dijo que, dados los obstáculos, es poco probable que se alcance un acuerdo a medio plazo. Los gasoductos Nord Stream están sujetos a sanciones por parte de EEUU y la UE, lo que haría ilegal cualquier reanudación del suministro. Trump podría suspender o suavizar las sanciones estadounidenses, pero si los demócratas obtienen el control del Congreso en las elecciones de mitad de legislatura del próximo mes, resultaría más difícil. Alemania y otros países europeos, que están invirtiendo miles de millones de euros en la reconstrucción de sus fuerzas armadas para defenderse de Rusia, se opondrían firmemente a la reapertura de Nord Stream. Una portavoz del Ministerio de Economía y Energía de Alemania señaló que Nord Stream y el gas ruso están sujetos a sanciones en Europa y que Alemania ha encontrado alternativas. Dijo que cualquier reapertura de los gasoductos requeriría la aprobación del Gobierno y que esto no era deseable. Antes de la invasión rusa de Ucrania en febrero de 2022, Alemania compraba más de la mitad de su gas a Rusia a través de los dos gasoductos Nord Stream, que quedaron inactivos después de que Moscú redujera el suministro a Europa y fueron destruidos en una serie de explosiones submarinas en septiembre de 2022. OBSTÁCULOS EN LA PROPIEDAD DE NORD STREAM Las conversaciones entre Moscú y Washington se desarrollan en un contexto de profunda desconfianza europea hacia los motivos de Rusia. A principios de este año, los jefes de cinco agencias de inteligencia europeas declararon a Reuters que Rusia no quería poner fin a la guerra rápidamente y que, en cambio, estaba utilizando las negociaciones con EEUU para impulsar acuerdos comerciales. Las relaciones entre Rusia y Alemania, uno de los principales proveedores de apoyo militar a Ucrania, han tocado fondo, ya que las autoridades de Berlín han acusado a Rusia de llevar a cabo una campaña sistemática de ataques híbridos. Algunos parlamentarios alemanes afirman que los acuerdos comerciales reforzarían a Moscú en su guerra contra Ucrania. "Esto amenaza con convertirse en un acuerdo sucio que le costará muy caro a Europa", dijo Michael Kellner, un diputado que estuvo a cargo de la política energética alemana tras la invasión de Ucrania. "Los estadounidenses y los rusos se repartirán los beneficios", añadió. Mientras que el Gobierno de coalición alemán se opone a la reactivación del gasoducto, Alternativa para Alemania (AfD), el partido político más popular del país, quiere que se lleve a cabo. Dmitriev se reunirá con los dirigentes de la AfD a principios del año que viene para debatir la reanudación de las ventas de gas ruso. Sin embargo, la venta de la propiedad de la empresa que controla los gasoductos Nord Stream a un inversor estadounidense o la reanudación del suministro de gas ruso se enfrentan a obstáculos. El gigante energético estatal ruso Gazprom posee el 51% de la empresa, mientras que otro 31% se reparte entre dos entidades alemanas y el resto está en manos de una empresa francesa y otra neerlandesa. Los dos accionistas alemanes pretenden conservar sus acciones para mantener la influencia alemana, en caso de que Gazprom vendiera su participación, según otra persona. Días después de las reuniones de Moscú, Kushner dijo en Kiev que había hablado con sus homólogos europeos sobre cómo la guerra había disparado los precios de la energía, abogando por "acuerdos de prosperidad" para fomentar la paz y dar a los "líderes algo por lo que ilusionarse". Aunque un acuerdo sobre el gas complacería al Kremlin, dividiría a la opinión pública alemana —que está dividida respecto a la compra de energía rusa— y a Europa, donde Polonia y los Estados bálticos son especialmente vulnerables a Rusia y rechazan los vínculos energéticos.

item.title: Südzucker verdient trotz stagnierender Umsätze mehr
item.description: Südzucker hat trotz stagnierender Erlöse einen deutlichen Gewinnsprung erzielt. Das operative Ergebnis (Ebitda) stieg im ersten Halbjahr des Geschäftsjahres 2026/27 auf 303 von 189 Millionen Euro im Vorjahreszeitraum, wie der Mannheimer SDax-Konzern am Donnerstag mitteilte. Der Usatz blieb in den sechs Monaten per Ende August mit 4,188 (Vorjahr: 4,199) Milliarden Euro nahezu unverändert. Im Segment Zucker halbierte sich der operative Verlust trotz niedrigerer Zuckerpreise und geringerer Absatzmengen nahezu auf 24 Millionen Euro. Der Konzern vermarktet neben Zucker unter anderem auch Glukosesirupe, Futtermittel, Stärke und Fruchtsaftkonzentrate.

Das operative Ergebnis (Ebitda) stieg im ersten Halbjahr des Geschäftsjahres 2026/27 auf 303 von 189 Millionen Euro im Vorjahreszeitraum, wie der Mannheimer SDax (.SDAXI) -Konzern am Donnerstag mitteilte. Der Usatz blieb in den sechs Monaten per Ende August mit 4,188 (Vorjahr: 4,199) Milliarden Euro nahezu unverändert. Im Segment Zucker halbierte sich der operative Verlust trotz niedrigerer Zuckerpreise und geringerer Absatzmengen nahezu auf 24 Millionen Euro. Der Konzern vermarktet neben Zucker unter anderem auch Glukosesirupe, Futtermittel, Stärke und Fruchtsaftkonzentrate. "Wir arbeiten in der gesamten Gruppe intensiv daran, unsere Effizienz zu steigern und Kosten entlang der gesamten Wertschöpfungskette weiter zu senken", erklärte Vorstandschef Niels Pörksen. Südzucker bestätigte seine Ende September [USN:L8N45K0EA TEXT:"angehobene Prognose"] für das am 28. Februar 2027 endende Geschäftsjahr. Der Konzern erwartet einen Umsatz von 8,3 bis 8,7 Milliarden Euro sowie ein Ebitda zwischen 540 und 680 Millionen Euro. Die Ernteaussichten belasten jedoch das Geschäft: Südzucker rechnet wegen anhaltender Hitze und Dürre insbesondere in Süddeutschland und Frankreich mit einer deutlich geringeren Zuckerproduktionsmenge als im Vorjahr. Pflanzenkrankheiten und Schädlingsbefall trübten zudem die Ertragsaussichten.

item.title: La Syrie envisage d'aider militairement Ryad - sources
item.description: La Syrie, proche alliée de l'Arabie saoudite, envisage de fournir une assistance militaire à Ryad dans la guerre au Yémen contre les Houthis, ont déclaré un responsable américain et une source militaire syrienne.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: La Syrie, proche alliée de l'Arabie saoudite, envisage de fournir une assistance militaire à Ryad dans la guerre au Yémen contre les Houthis, ont déclaré un responsable américain et une source militaire syrienne. Cette assistance pourrait prendre la forme de moyens de défense pour aider le royaume à se protéger des attaques de la milice soutenue par l'Iran, ou d'un déploiement de militaires pour des opérations offensives aux côtés des forces gouvernementales yéménites, ont dit ces sources. Selon le responsable américain, l'Arabie saoudite a demandé que la Syrie envoie des forces pour combattre les Houthis. En réponse à une demande de commentaires adressée au ministère des Affaires étrangères syrien, un diplomate syrien a déclaré que la Syrie se tenait aux côtés de l'Arabie saoudite face aux attaques des Houthis, tout en ajoutant que le gouvernement se concentrait avant tout sur des priorités nationales telles que la reconstruction après la guerre civile. "Si l'Arabie saoudite venait à solliciter une coopération militaire ou un échange d'expertise, cela se ferait exclusivement par les voies officielles et dans le cadre des accords bilatéraux régissant les relations entre nos deux pays frères", a déclaré ce diplomate dans un communiqué. Le gouvernement saoudien et le ministre yéménite de l'Information n'ont pas répondu aux demandes de commentaires. L'Arabie saoudite a requis l'assistance de nombreux pays, des Etats-Unis à l'Europe et au Moyen-Orient, pour renforcer ses moyens défensifs et offensifs face aux Houthis, qui ont annoncé en juillet un blocus maritime des exportations pétrolières saoudiennes et progressé de manière spectaculaire vers le détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, vital pour le trafic de pétrole. L'armée yéménite, épaulée depuis 2015 par les moyens aériens de l'Arabie saoudite et d'autres pays du Golfe, a lancé lundi une contre-offensive pour reconquérir le terrain perdu ces dernières semaines, avec des gains limités pour le moment. Le président syrien Ahmed al Charaa s'est rendu mardi à Ryad, où il a rencontré le prince héritier Mohamed ben Salmane. Le sujet de l'assistance militaire a été abordé, selon la source américaine. L'ancien chef rebelle a été raccompagné à son avion par le ministre de la Défense Khalid ben Salmane, frère du prince héritier en charge du dossier yéménite. Les combattants des groupes d'opposition syriens qui ont lutté contre le régime de Bachar al Assad, depuis le début de la guerre civile en 2011 jusqu'à sa chute en décembre 2024, ont été recrutés ces dernières années comme mercenaires dans d'autres conflits, en Libye par exemple ou dans la guerre russo-ukrainienne. PARI RISQUÉ L'envoi de troupes n'en serait pas moins un pari risqué pour l'actuel gouvernement de Damas. Le nouvel Etat syrien, qui a adopté une politique de non-engagement dans les conflits et entend se consacrer à la reconstruction du pays, s'efforce de constituer une seule armée à partir des nombreux groupes armés de l'ancienne rébellion, qui comprennent des milices sunnites radicales, tout en s'employant à contenir les tensions avec les communautés minoritaires, dont celle des Alaouites, minorité issue du chiisme à laquelle appartient le clan Assad. Un conflit entre l'armée syrienne et les Houthis, eux-mêmes une minorité chiite, porterait le risque d'exacerber les tensions religieuses, ce que souhaitent ni Damas ni ses partenaires occidentaux, a souligné le responsable américain. Fournir une aide militaire à l'Arabie saoudite pourrait aussi être considéré comme un acte hostile par l'Iran et ses alliés chiites du Hezbollah au Liban et les milices chiites en Irak. Dans le même temps, Ahmed al Charaa tient à afficher son soutien à Mohamed ben Salmane, qui a joué un rôle capital pour aider l'ancien chef djihadiste à acquérir une légitimité sur la scène internationale, en organisant notamment, en mai 2025, une rencontre entre le président syrien et son homologue américain Donald Trump. Ryad fournit en outre une aide financière à la Syrie qui pourrait être augmentée, fait valoir le responsable américain. Pour H.A. Hellyer, chercheur associé principal au Royal United Services Institute de Londres, "une nouvelle Syrie envoyant un contingent défensif très restreint vers les lieux les plus sacrés du monde islamique, tout en apportant un soutien technique pour neutraliser les drones, aurait une portée symbolique extrêmement positive". "En revanche, toute mesure allant au-delà, notamment le déploiement de troupes syriennes au sol, constituerait selon moi une tout autre affaire - une option que Damas chercherait probablement à éviter, compte tenu des priorités sur lesquelles le pays doit se concentrer en interne."

item.title: German exports fall unexpectedly in August
item.description: German exports unexpectedly in August due to sharp decline in exports to the United States.
item.dc:creator: Maria Martinez
item.content:encoded: German exports unexpectedly in August due to sharp decline in exports to the United States. Exports fell by 0.8% compared with the previous month, data from the federal statistics office showed on Thursday. The result compared with a forecast 0.6% increase in a Reuters poll. Imports were up 0.9% on a calendar and seasonally adjusted basis compared with July. As a result, the trade surplus narrowed to €19.5 billion ($21.82 billion) in August from €21.6 billion in July. Exports to EU countries dropped by 0.6% on the month, while exports to countries outside the EU decreased by 1.1%. Exports to the United States fell by 6.3% on July, while exports to the United Kingdom increased by 16.7%. Meanwhile, exports to China rose by 4.7% but imports increased by 11.0%. ($1 = 0.8935 euros)

item.title: Britain's Tesco raises profit outlook floor after first-half rise
item.description: Tesco , Britain's largest food retailer, lifted the bottom end of its full-year profit outlook on Thursday after reporting a 6.5% increase for its first half, even as a very hot summer weighed on sales volumes across the industry.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tesco (TSCO.L) , Britain's largest food retailer, lifted the bottom end of its full-year profit outlook on Thursday after reporting a 6.5% increase for its first half, even as a very hot summer weighed on sales volumes across the industry. The group, which has a [USN:L8N4560GY TEXT:"UK grocery market share"] of 28%, said it made an adjusted operating profit of £1.783 billion ($2.35 billion) for the 26 weeks to August 29, on sales, excluding VAT sales tax and fuel, up 2.0% to £33.8 billion. UK like-for-like sales for the half rose 1.5%, having been up 1.8% in the [USN:L8N42Q06U TEXT:"first quarter"]. Monthly industry data has shown Tesco lost a little market share in the second quarter. However, it was up against a tough comparative performance in the same quarter last year when UK like-for-like sales rose 4.6%, helped by disruption at competitors Marks & Spencer (MKS.L) , the Co-op and Asda. The conflict in the Middle East, and its impact on energy prices, also created uncertainty for many households during the first half. Tesco, whose shares have risen 8% so far this year, is now forecasting adjusted operating profit of £3.15 billion to £3.3 billion ($4.16-$4.36 billion) for its year to end-February 2027, versus previous guidance of £3.0 billion to £3.3 billion and £3.152 billion made in 2025/26. ($1 = 0.7577 pounds)

item.title: China's funding of development institutions is up sharply, but its power still lags, study shows
item.description: China, the world's second-largest economy, has boosted funding of multilateral development institutions tenfold since 2010, but its voting power and presence in international bodies still lag its economic weight, a new study released on Thursday said.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: China, the world's second-largest economy, has boosted funding of multilateral development institutions tenfold since 2010, but its voting power and presence in international bodies still lag its economic weight, a new study released on Thursday said. Beijing's funding for development banks reached $3 billion in 2024 while its funding for UN development-related bodies surged by 47%, according to the report by the Center for Global Development. China also sharply increased its funding for multilateral climate finance to $5.25 billion in 2025, but slashed its support for funds like Gavi, a public-private partnership to procure and distribute vaccines in low-income countries, by 32%. "This is a big step up from 15 years ago, but it's still a tiny share of China's economy," said Ian Mitchell, co-author of the report, noting China's funding decisions had been quite selective. "It hasn't supported much of the UN voluntarily. It hasn't supported the verticals virtually at all, and it's continued its bilateral efforts, but at a smaller scale," he said. Co-author Beata Cichocka said China has made some large contributions to the World Health Organization while the US withdrew from the body, but Beijing was not filling all the gaps left by Washington and other Western powers, many of which have cut development outlays. China has long pushed for a bigger role at the World Bank and IMF to better reflect its size and contributions. China's share of the World Bank of around 6% is less than half what the fund's own economic formula suggests, while the US retains veto power with its shareholding of around 16%. US and other Western officials have put the brakes on changes to the shareholder structures of the IMF and World Bank that would give China a larger voting power, arguing there is no consensus on realignments and China lacks transparency. The study, released ahead of the annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok next week, showed China was now the fifth-largest donor to the World Bank's fund for the poorest countries, the International Development Association, following a $1.5 billion pledge during the last replenishment. China also boosted funding for zero- and low-interest multilateral bank lending programs by 92% in the last five years, it said. Only 11% of Beijing's contributions to UN entities were voluntary, which Mitchell called a telling sign of China's strategic emphasis. Over 70% of US contributions were voluntary. Chinese nationals hold five senior management jobs at the World Bank and other multilateral development banks, a number that has held steady since 2021. But Beijing has lost top jobs at several UN institutions since 2020, including the WHO and the International Telecommunication Union, the study found. China, close to being declared a high-income country, has sharply reduced its borrowing from development banks, with total borrowing down to $4.7 billion in 2024 from $8 billion in 2021, the study found. Once the World Bank's biggest borrower in 2017, it now ranks 18th, and the Bank recently announced that it will [USN:FWN43216V TEXT:"stop all lending to China after 2031."]

item.content:encoded: Daimler Truck (DTGGe.DE) reported 26% growth in third-quarter vehicle sales on Thursday, as deliveries increased at both its North American unit and largely Europe-based Mercedes-Benz Trucks, offering an early indication that the stronger second half of the year forecast by the management was taking shape. item.title: China border town can't shake the blues despite promise of bridge to North Korea
item.description: Chinese taxi driver Wang peered through binoculars at a North Korean flag fluttering beyond a soon-to-open bridge linking his city of Dandong with the secretive nation.
item.dc:creator: David Kirton, Huey Leong
item.content:encoded: Chinese taxi driver Wang peered through binoculars at a North Korean flag fluttering beyond a soon-to-open bridge linking his city of Dandong with the secretive nation. "They finally finished their side," said the 40-year-old, one of dozens who gathered this week near the New Yalu River Bridge in the northeastern city, amid rumours that its opening will soon end a 12-year delay. Coffee shops, a fun fair and a Little Yellow Duck theme park are springing up nearby, suggesting the struggling city hopes to cash in on the new link, but some residents and shopkeepers saw it more as a curiosity than an economic boon. "It won't bring much new business here as regular citizens can't visit, but they're still our friends," Wang told Reuters during a visit on Tuesday, the 77th anniversary of the neighbours' diplomatic ties, referring to North Koreans. While China completed the bridge in 2014, hoping to boost trade ties, North Korea left its approach roads and customs facilities unfinished as relations soured over Pyongyang's nuclear tests and the U.N. sanctions that followed. Work resumed after a thaw in ties led to a June visit by Chinese President Xi Jinping, with both capitals having restored train services and direct flights, though neither has set a date to open the bridge. The North Korean customs house appeared complete, while green signs were lit up over the gate on the Chinese side, though no traffic crossed. The opening of the new bridge would show progress in ties , within weeks of North Korea opening its first [USN:L6N44Z0AS TEXT:"road bridge"] with Russia. FADED BORDER TOWN The bridge delay was a setback for Dandong, whose economy thrived in the early 21st century as the primary trade gateway to North Korea's isolated economy. For now, most goods still cross about 10 km (6 miles) upstream at an 83-year-old bridge with a rail track and a single-lane road. That remains the busiest of about 15 crossing points along the roughly 1,350-km (840-mile) border. Recovering trade ties carried China's exports to North Korea to a six-year high of $2.3 billion last year, or an annual increase of 25%, though still well short of levels before the UN sanctions in 2017. The uptick appears to have brought little benefit to Dandong, whose economy grew just 0.3% in the first half of the year against a national figure of 4.7%, with investment falling a third and new home sales down 28%, city data shows. Although government offices in the city moved in 2011 to the Dandong New Zone near the new bridge, the area remains largely residential, with many apartments vacant. Low pay was one reason why few workers stick around, said Wang, the taxi driver, adding that factory jobs in the locality pay only about 3,000 yuan ($420) a month. 'CUT OFF FROM THE WORLD' There is also little optimism for an economic revival at a trade zone in Dandong called Guomenwan that is just a five-minute drive from the Chinese side of the new bridge. Launched in 2015 with a reported investment of 1 billion yuan ($140 million), the complex now has mostly empty storefronts, with cafes, a vet clinic and a gym targeting the domestic market. "This doesn't have much to do with us," a manager of the complex said, when asked about the bridge opening, speaking on condition of anonymity. In its first few years, the zone imported large volumes of North Korean seafood and farm products, he said. But subsequent UN Security Council resolutions banned such imports, as well as sales of steel and industrial machinery to Pyongyang. "Business is slow here," said Chen, a seller of curtains and fabric. "There aren't that many people doing up their homes." Business was mostly local, added Chen, who gave only her surname, though she sometimes sees Chinese from ethnic Korean backgrounds working as middlemen, and the occasional North Korean buyer accompanied by an interpreter. Yet tourists still throng steadily to Dandong to gaze across the river, gathering at the old bridge where merchants sell snacks and offer enticements such as games of ring toss. But there the journey stops. North Korea has not reopened to Chinese tourists since sealing its borders in 2020. "They've cut themselves off from the world," said Zhang, a passerby at the new bridge. "It would be better to do more business with South Korea."

item.title: Singapore Grand Prix entertainment may be curbed if haze worsens, FIA says
item.description: There might be "some restrictions" on outdoor activity such as entertainment during this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix, but not on the race, if the haze currently blanketing the city-state worsens, the motor sports governing body said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Xinghui Kok
item.content:encoded: There might be "some restrictions" on outdoor activity such as entertainment during this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix, but not on the race, if the haze currently blanketing the city-state worsens, the motor sports governing body said on Thursday. Singapore has been shrouded in smoke for weeks, with the air quality currently in the "unhealthy" range across the country, just a day ahead of the race weekend and during a [USN:L4N45O0GO TEXT:"busy week of conferences"] with regional, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders descending on Singapore. Despite the pall from Indonesia's most [USN:L6N4580KB TEXT:"intense fires"] in over a decade, the haze and poor air quality are not expected to threaten track activity or the staging of the F1 night race, said a spokesperson from the Federation Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA). "Air quality levels are being monitored by the relevant local authorities, and appropriate contingency measures are in place," said the spokesperson. The FIA did not give a threshold for when plans affecting entertainment and other outdoor activity would be activated. The spokesperson said they were following recommendations from local authorities and working closely with them to safeguard the health of F1 teams. Singapore's National Environment Agency and tourism board did not immediately respond to a request for comment. On Wednesday evening, the environment agency's haze update said: "Under the prevailing southeasterly to southerly winds, smoke haze from these areas may continue to drift towards Singapore." In 2019, when haze was similarly in the "unhealthy" range during the Singapore Grand Prix, organisers had first aid help on standby and made N95 masks available to those who needed it.

item.title: People in Russian-occupied Ukrainian town risk 'road of death' to get food
item.description: Trapped and facing starvation, residents of the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine risk their lives to travel for hours by foot and bicycle along mine-strewn roads to get food and water.
item.dc:creator: Yuliia Dysa
item.content:encoded: Trapped and facing starvation, residents of the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine risk their lives to travel for hours by foot and bicycle along mine-strewn roads to get food and water. The main route out of the town, lying near the front line east of the Dnipro River, heads deeper into Russian-controlled areas. It is littered with burned-out cars and charred by blasts, according to witnesses, relatives, humanitarian groups and video footage verified by Reuters. Attack drones prowl overhead. Residents say the last food deliveries to a local store took place in May. "What on earth could possibly be left in your house when you haven't been to the shop for half a year?" a woman living in the town told Reuters, asking not to be identified for fear of reprisals from Russian occupying forces. She had recently attempted the trip to Radensk, some 20 km (12.5 miles) to the southeast. On her way back, she was injured by a landmine. "There is no safe way out," she said afterwards, adding that a few days earlier three people had been killed on the same route, which some locals call "the road of death". Reuters was not able to verify the woman's account independently, although it chimes with those from other witnesses, officials and aid workers familiar with the humanitarian crisis in Oleshky. That people are even attempting these journeys points to growing desperation. "The choice Russia forces on civilians every day: to stay — and starve to death; or to leave - and risk being blown up by a landmine," Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said. He also said Kyiv had offered a local ceasefire and evacuation routes to residents who wanted to leave but that Russia had rejected the proposal. Russia has acknowledged critical problems with food and medical supplies in Oleshky and said its military was working to resolve them. It blamed Ukraine for the crisis, saying it was obstructing those supplies getting to the town. 'THEY KNOW THEY ARE DOOMED' Oleshky in Ukraine's Kherson region, with a pre-war population of some 24,000, is still home to around 1,700 residents, including 47 children, according to Danielle Bell, head of the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine. Drone footage from the town shared by Ukraine's 34th Separate Marine Brigade "Borysfen" and verified by Reuters shows residential and administrative buildings ruined and abandoned after more than four years of war and Russian occupation. There is no stable power, water or heating. Movement in and out is more dangerous than ever. Tetiana Hasanenko, head of the local military administration sitting in the Ukraine-controlled part of the region, keeps in regular contact with Oleshky locals. "They know they are doomed. These are terrible words to say, but they know they will die either from hunger or from strikes," she told Reuters in late September. Ukrainian troops do not have direct access to the town. In recent days, the Ukrainian military said it had dropped food to residents using drones. Reuters could not independently confirm those claims and some residents expressed scepticism, saying they had seen nothing. Andrii Sybiha, Ukraine's foreign minister, said Russia, as the aggressor state, bore "full responsibility for this humanitarian disaster." Russia's defence ministry and the Russian-installed authorities in occupied Kherson did not respond to requests for comment. FEAR OF HUNGER Oleshky residents said food supplies became unreliable late last year, but the situation deteriorated significantly after May. Before then, Ukrainian volunteers were able to take in food and evacuate people. Since then, people have largely lived off the land, and that is becoming untenable as winter approaches. Larysa, a Ukrainian woman who fled Oleshky shortly after Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022, told Reuters in London that her husband was still there and surviving on dwindling rations. The 72-year-old, who declined to give her full name or that of her husband out of concern for his safety, said he was living on vegetables and homemade flatbread cooked on an open fire. He was using pre-invasion flour stocks that had gone bad long ago. "He's been living on this for the whole summer, ever since May. There are no eggs, no dairy, no meat – there's nothing," his wife said. He feeds their four cats and a dog with grass mixed with whatever grain is left. Larysa said she had "forbidden" her husband from taking the road out of Oleshky to Radensk in search of food, describing the journey as a life-and-death gamble, or "Russian roulette". The Ukrainian brigade footage shows dozens of burnt-out and abandoned vehicles along the route. The buildings on either side have been badly damaged. Larysa is sure her husband hides the full extent of his difficulties when they speak briefly by phone twice a week. As winter sets in, homegrown staples like cucumbers, courgettes and tomatoes are running out and fear of starvation grows. "There really isn't anything left to swap. We've used it all up," the woman injured by the mine said. The only way to boil water is over an open fire because gas cylinders are impossible to get. Medicines are out of date and she eats just once a day - a thin piece of flatbread with tomato and salt or honey.

item.title: Battle for Mideast oil market share has already begun
item.description: Middle East oil producers have launched a battle to recapture market share lost during the Iran war, setting current and former OPEC members on a collision course as traffic through the Strait of Hormuz gradually recovers. Such turf battles usually send crude prices plummeting, yet consumers are unlikely to see much relief at the pump in the near term.
item.dc:creator: Ron Bousso
item.content:encoded: Middle East oil producers have launched a battle to recapture market share lost during the Iran war, setting current and former OPEC members on a collision course as traffic through the Strait of Hormuz gradually recovers. Such turf battles usually send crude prices plummeting, yet consumers are unlikely to see much relief at the pump in the near term. The Iran war , now in its eighth month, delivered the biggest shock to the global oil market in decades. After Iran imposed a blockade on the [USN:S8N43Z006 TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"] – through which roughly a fifth of global oil supplies once flowed – Gulf producers, including Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait and Iraq, were cut off from their most important export route. While some quickly shifted volumes to alternative routes bypassing Hormuz, regional exports remained well below pre-war levels for months. That is beginning to change. Crude exports through Hormuz have averaged 12 million barrels per day over the past two weeks, around 80% of pre-war levels, according to data analytics firm Kpler. When combining Hormuz volumes with shipments through alternative routes, including Saudi Arabia's Red Sea terminals and the UAE's Fujairah export hub, Middle East crude exports exceeded the pre-war average of 18 million bpd for much of the week ending October 3, according to Kpler. As a result, the global crude supply deficit is expected to narrow to just 250,000 bpd in October from almost 4 million bpd in May, according to consultancy Energy Aspects. The Strait of Hormuz remains far from safe, however. Iranian forces continue to target vessels moving through the narrow waterway, with nearly [USN:L1N45T0HL TEXT:"one tanker hit every day"] over the past two weeks. But Gulf producers are increasingly willing to accept this risk, as well as the sky-high shipping and insurance costs, to maximize their exports and rebuild ties with customers forced to seek alternative suppliers during the disruption. This has nevertheless kept benchmark [USN:L6N45Q087 TEXT:"Brent oil prices elevated"] at over $100 a barrel, around 40% above pre-war levels. It appears the first shot in the Mideast market share war has already been fired. OPEC UNDER PRESSURE Oil market share battles in the [USN:L6N45Q01R TEXT:"OPEC"] era have historically occurred following the discovery of new sources of supply, such as offshore drilling in the 1980s or the shale revolution in the 2010s. In response to perceived threats to its market dominance, the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries has typically reacted by allowing low-cost producers to ramp up output in an attempt to squeeze rivals. This time, however, the battle is undermining the group from within. OPEC, already reeling from the war early in the year, was dealt another heavy blow in May when the UAE withdrew from the group to pursue plans for a substantial increase in production capacity. The move raised questions about whether the 66-year-old Saudi-led club could emerge from the conflict with its influence intact and reassert its ability to manage prices through coordinated supply control. The seemingly uncoordinated, fragmented response of Gulf producers to the Iran conflict suggests that control may no longer exist. RETURN OF THE MARKET SHARE WAR The recent rebound in exports is encouraging Gulf states to raise production rapidly. Combined crude production in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Iraq and Kuwait is expected to average 17.3 million bpd in October, compared with about 21 million bpd in the six months before the war, according to Energy Aspects. The recovery, however, is uneven. The UAE, having rapidly developed the complex Hormuz shuttle system, has exported an average 3.3 million bpd of crude since June, broadly matching pre-war levels, according to Kpler. At the same time, UAE production has averaged around 4.2 million bpd since June, above its pre-war average of 3.9 million bpd, according to Energy Aspects. Saudi Arabia's path has been more complicated. Riyadh initially redirected large volumes of crude to its west coast port of Yanbu following the outbreak of the war, enabling exports to remain near 60% of pre-war levels during much of the conflict. But attacks on the East-West pipeline in September, combined with a Houthi blockade of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait used for exports, disrupted that strategy and forced the kingdom to shift more exports back through Hormuz. The move has proven successful. Saudi crude exports have averaged about 7.3 million bpd over the past three weeks, close to pre-war levels, according to Kpler. Production, however, remains significantly lower. Saudi output is expected to average just 7.4 million bpd in October, roughly 75% of pre-war levels, reflecting reduced domestic refining capacity following strikes on processing facilities in recent months. Saudi Aramco's (2223.SE) CEO Amin Nasser this week told the Energy Intelligence Forum conference in London that the kingdom could increase its production to 12 million bpd within days if needed. Recovery levels vary widely among the other Gulf producers, with a notable ramp-up in production in Iraq. A FRAGILE RECOVERY The impact of increased Middle Eastern production is beginning to show up in Asia, the destination for most Gulf crude exports. Saudi Arabia's share of Asian crude imports fell from 24% in February to a record low of 9% in September but is expected to recover to around 14% in October, according to ROI calculations based on Kpler data. The UAE largely maintained its position, with its share of Asian imports slipping only slightly from 13% in February to 12% in October. The biggest loser has been Iran. Iranian crude sales have effectively collapsed since the United States imposed a naval blockade on the country's exports. Iran's share of Asian crude imports fell from a one-year high of 6% in March to zero in October. The scramble to recover lost customers is becoming a defining feature of the post-blockade market. Gulf producers, eager to replenish state coffers after more than seven months of disruption, are increasing exports while some producers, including Iraq and [USN:S8N45108K TEXT:"Saudi Arabia"], have [USN:L1N45N03W TEXT:"offered deep discounts"] to buyers willing to load cargoes inside the Gulf. But will this result in dramatically lower prices at the pump? Probably not as long as getting oil through Hormuz remains this [USN:L6N45Q087 TEXT:"risky, unpredictable and expensive"]. The Mideast oil export recovery rests on fragile foundations, but Gulf producers appear willing to forge ahead with their own battle regardless. Die Koalition sei sich einig, dass wirtschaftliches Wachstum, sichere Arbeitsplätze und der gesellschaftliche Zusammenhalt im Zentrum des weiteren Arbeitsprogramms stünden. "Deshalb hat der Koalitionsausschuss sämtliche aktuellen Themen besprochen, um die damit verbundenen Vorhaben zügig zum Abschluss zu bringen." Die Koalitionsspitzen hatten am Mittwochabend viereinhalb Stunden beraten. Das Treffen diente vor allem der Rückversicherung beider Seiten, dass man noch zu den im Juli verabredeten Reformprojekten steht. Im Vorfeld war bereits betont worden, dass man keine neuen Beschlüsse treffen wolle. Zuletzt hatte es in der schwarz-roten Koalition neue Diskussionen über die geplanten strukturellen Reformen in der Pflegeversicherung und über die Höhe der Zuckersteuer gegeben.

item.title: Bank of Japan sees broadening inflationary pressure
item.description: The Bank of Japan said on Thursday price increases driven by higher raw material costs were spreading to consumer goods with some firms hiking prices more frequently than in the past, signaling its concern over broadening inflationary pressure.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Japan said on Thursday price increases driven by higher raw material costs were spreading to consumer goods with some firms hiking prices more frequently than in the past, signaling its concern over broadening inflationary pressure. The central bank also offered an upbeat view on the economic outlook, saying brisk AI-related demand was increasing domestic output for electronic goods, machinery and telecommunication infrastructure. "Many regions saw firms passing on a broad range of rising costs," including higher raw material costs from the Middle East conflict and the weak yen, as well as increasing labour costs, the BOJ said in a statement released after a quarterly meeting of its regional branch managers. The BOJ raised its economic assessment for two of the country's nine regions and maintained its view for the remaining areas, saying they were all recovering moderately. Given volatile moves in input costs, some firms are raising prices more frequently than in the past, the statement said. "Efforts to pass-through rising costs are spreading to firms close to consumers," leading to more companies raising prices, the statement said.

item.title: TSMC's third-quarter revenue surges to record, beating market forecast
item.description: TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, reported on Thursday record third-quarter revenue of T$1.49 trillion ($46.71 billion), beating the market forecast and rising 50% from the year-earlier period due to surging demand for AI applications.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, reported on Thursday record third-quarter revenue of T$1.49 trillion ($46.71 billion), beating the market forecast and rising 50% from the year-earlier period due to surging demand for AI applications. Revenue in the July-September quarter of this year came in at T$1.49 trillion, according to Reuters calculations, compared with T$989.92 billion in the year-ago period. An LSEG SmartEstimate, drawn from 19 analysts, had predicted third-quarter revenue of T$1.46 trillion. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) (2330.TW) , is a major supplier to companies, including Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Apple (AAPL.O) . In July, on its last [USN:L1N43I00B TEXT:"earnings call"], the company predicted third-quarter revenue of between $44.6 billion and $45.8 billion. The company gives its forecast only in US dollars and not in Taiwan dollars. For September alone, TSMC reported that revenue rose 54.6% year-on-year to T$511.86 billion. [USN:L1N45T115 TEXT:"Samsung Electronics"] (005930.KS) earlier on Thursday projected its quarterly operating profit would top 100 trillion won, a world first for a technology company, estimating a nearly nine-fold jump in third-quarter earnings as booming demand for AI chips drove strong memory sales. TSMC, Asia's most valuable publicly listed company with a market capitalisation of $2.1 trillion, did not provide any details or forward guidance in its brief revenue statement. It is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings next Thursday, where it will also update its outlook and plans for the current quarter and the rest of the year. TSMC is expected to report a 64% on-year rise in third- quarter net profit to T$740.8 billion, according to an LSEG SmartEstimate. TSMC's Taipei-listed shares closed down 1.35% on Thursday ahead of the release of the revenue data. The broader market (.TWII) closed down 1%. The shares have risen 64.52% so far this year, in line with the broader market. ($1 = 31.9020 Taiwan dollars)

item.title: USA/MIDTERMS-Trump au Texas, bastion républicain où le scrutin s'annonce serré
item.description: Le président américain Donald Trump s'est rendu mercredi au Texas pour la troisième fois en un mois afin de faire campagne en faveur des républicains, qui se retrouvent engagés dans des scrutins de mi-mandat plus serrés que prévu.
item.dc:creator: Nandita Bose
item.content:encoded: Le président américain Donald Trump s'est rendu mercredi au Texas pour la troisième fois en un mois afin de faire campagne en faveur des républicains, qui se retrouvent engagés dans des scrutins de mi-mandat plus serrés que prévu. Devant une salle comble à San Antonio, Donald Trump a affiché son soutien au candidat républicain au Sénat Ken Paxton, qui est au coude à coude avec le démocrate James Talarico. Une défaite le 3 novembre compliquerait la tâche du parti pour conserver sa faible majorité au Sénat et marquerait un revers majeur dans ce bastion républicain. Donald Trump a salué la loyauté de Ken Paxton, à qui il avait apporté son soutien lors des primaires du parti dans l'Etat après avoir reproché au sénateur républicain sortant, John Cornyn, de ne pas l'avoir soutenu dans les moments difficiles. "Il a été à nos côtés tout du long", a dit le locataire de la Maison blanche au sujet de Ken Paxton. "C'est un homme fantastique et il a fait un travail formidable." Ses partisans, dont certains agitaient des chapeaux de cow-boy, ont acclamé Donald Trump et crié "USA", couvrant les voix de plusieurs manifestants qui ont interrompu l’événement. Donald Trump a déclaré que les manifestants devaient "ficher le camp d'ici". Les déplacements répétés de Donald Trump au Texas s'inscrivent dans le cadre d'une campagne plus large menée dans les Etats à tendance républicaine où les scrutins pour les élections de mi-mandat s'annoncent serrés. Donald Trump s'est déjà rendu au Texas, en Oklahoma, en Alabama, en Ohio et au Nebraska, tandis que le vice-président J.D. Vance a fait campagne en Alaska. Les candidats républicains sont en difficulté dans plusieurs Etats, alors que les électeurs se concentrent sur les questions de la hausse des coûts de la vie et de la guerre en l'Iran. Un nouveau sondage Reuters/Ipsos souligne l'ampleur du défi auquel sont confrontés les républicains : la cote de popularité de Donald Trump reste bloquée à un plus bas historique de 32%, tandis que les électeurs inscrits préfèrent les démocrates aux républicains (44% contre 37%) à l'approche du scrutin. item.title: Brewers KO Padres in Game 4, set up NLCS rematch vs. Dodgers
item.description: Jackson Chourio delivered the tiebreaking single and Garrett Mitchell robbed a potential game-tying homer in the eighth inning to help the Milwaukee Brewers advance to the National League Championship Series with a 3-1 road victory over the San Diego Padres in Game 4 on Wednesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jackson Chourio delivered the tiebreaking single and Garrett Mitchell robbed a potential game-tying homer in the eighth inning to help the Milwaukee Brewers advance to the National League Championship Series with a 3-1 road victory over the San Diego Padres in Game 4 on Wednesday night. Aaron Ashby (1-0) tossed three innings of scoreless, hitless relief for the Brewers, who halted their major-league-record-tying 12-game postseason road losing streak dating back to 2018. Ashby struck out three and walked two in a 38-pitch effort as Milwaukee finished off the best-of-five NL Division Series with a three-games-to-one edge. Milwaukee will face the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS for the second straight season. The Dodgers swept the four-game set last year when the Brewers scored just four runs. Mitchell had two hits, an RBI and a run in addition to his big defensive play. Sal Frelick scored once and had an RBI, William Contreras had two hits, and Jake Bauers went 1-for-1 with three walks and a run. Fernando Tatis Jr. homered in the third inning for the Padres. The only other San Diego hits came in the first inning, when Jackson Merrill singled and Manny Machado followed with a bunt single. The Padres wound up leaving the bases loaded without scoring in that frame. San Diego had one on and one out in the eighth inning when Machado hit a deep drive to center off Abner Uribe. Mitchell jumped above the wall to make the catch and thwart Machado's bid for a tying homer. Trevor Megill struck out two in a perfect ninth for his second save of the series. He also was the winner when Milwaukee rallied to take Game 2. The score was tied at 1 when Mitchell tripled just inside the first base line off Robbie Ray (0-1) to start the fifth. One out later, Chourio ripped a liner over the head of reliever Bradgley Rodriguez and into center field to give the Brewers a 2-1 lead. The hit gave the 22-year-old Chourio 17 career postseason RBIs, breaking the franchise mark previously held by Ryan Braun. In the sixth, Bauers hit a leadoff single off Jason Adam and Cooper Pratt followed with a ground-rule double into the left field corner. Frelick followed with a sacrifice fly to left to score Bauers and give Milwaukee a two-run edge. Milwaukee pushed across a run in the top of the third against Padres starter Walker Buehler. Frelick reached on an infield single, stole second and scored on Mitchell's line single to center. San Diego knotted the score in the bottom of the inning when Tatis sent a 429-foot blast to center off Brewers starter Robert Gasser. Gasser allowed one run and three hits over four innings. He struck out three and walked one. Buehler gave up one run on three hits over three-plus innings. He walked two and fanned none. --Field Level Media

item.title: USA-Les responsables de la Fed divisés sur la justification de la hausse des taux-"minutes"
item.description: Les responsables de la Réserve fédérale (Fed) ont divergé le mois dernier sur le raisonnement justifiant de relever les taux d'intérêt, certains d'entre eux notant la nécessité de contrer le choc énergétique tandis que d'autres, plus conservateurs, ayant dit avant tout vouloir lutter contre l'inflation.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les responsables de la Réserve fédérale (Fed) ont divergé le mois dernier sur le raisonnement justifiant de relever les taux d'intérêt, certains d'entre eux notant la nécessité de contrer le choc énergétique tandis que d'autres, plus conservateurs, ayant dit avant tout vouloir lutter contre l'inflation. D'après le compte-rendu publié mercredi de la réunion des 15-16 septembre de la Fed, lors de laquelle la banque centrale américaine a voté à l'unanimité pour [USN:L8N4581JU TEXT:"une hausse des taux"] de 25 points de base, ses membres ont débattu de la logique de ce resserrement monétaire. L'idée que la mesure soit avant tout une précaution a été mise en avant par "certains" responsables, est-il indiqué, quand d'autres se sont interrogés sur la perspective que ce relèvement des taux marque le début d'un cycle de resserrement monétaire. "De nombreux participants ont souligné qu'un relèvement de l'objectif des taux serait prudent pour gérer les risques, fournir des garanties contre l'inflation qui demeure de manière persistante au-dessus de l'objectif en raison d'une demande plus solide qu'attendu", est-il écrit dans les 'minutes'. Toutefois, d'autres responsables de la Fed ont dit voir la hausse des taux approuvée le mois dernier comme une mesure importante pour empêcher principalement le choc énergétique d'avoir de larges répercussions sur les prix. Selon le compte-rendu de la réunion, "plusieurs participants ont dit considérer la politique actuelle des taux comme non-restrictive ou légèrement restrictive seulement". "La plupart des participants ont établi qu'une hausse supplémentaire (...) sera vraisemblablement appropriée d'ici la fin de l'année", est-il ajouté dans le document.

item.title: India denies bias in satellite internet approvals after Musk's 'oligarchs' jab
item.description: India defended its satellite internet approval process as fair and non-discriminatory on Thursday, hours after billionaire Elon Musk accused unnamed "oligarchs" of blocking Starlink's launch in the South Asian nation.
item.dc:creator: Munsif Vengattil
item.content:encoded: India defended its satellite internet approval process as fair and non-discriminatory on Thursday, hours after billionaire Elon Musk accused unnamed "oligarchs" of blocking Starlink's launch in the South Asian nation. Starlink was being blocked by "certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people," Musk wrote on X, without naming anyone. India's telecom market is dominated by billionaires Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio and Sunil Mittal's Bharti Airtel. Their satellite internet ventures, alongside Musk's Starlink, have secured early approvals to launch in India but are awaiting spectrum assignment and final clearances. Airtel and Jio did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The wait has stretched on for four years for Starlink, following scrutiny over security requirements and access to spectrum. Responding to Musk's comments, India's telecommunications ministry said three entities were at broadly the same regulatory stage, with security assessments under way for each. It did not name the companies or Musk. "The suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived," the ministry said in a statement. The clash is not new. Musk has previously been [USN:L4N38E0RQ TEXT:"at odds"] with Mittal and Ambani over how India should grant them spectrum, before the three [USN:L4N3PV05S TEXT:"set aside"] their differences in 2025 to sign separate deals to distribute Starlink devices in India. India offers Starlink, part of Musk's SpaceX, access to a satellite broadband market that Deloitte has forecast will be worth $1.9 billion by 2030. The timing adds a diplomatic layer: the US has pushed Starlink's market access as a goodwill marker in trade talks with tariff-hit countries, and New Delhi and Washington [USN:L4N45S0BG TEXT:"have struggled"] to finalise a trade deal since reaching a framework in February. Security concerns have also followed the recovery of Starlink equipment in India. Indian authorities have said they found Starlink devices in two separate operations in late 2024: a drug seizure by police in the Andaman and Nicobar islands and an army search in Manipur state. Musk then said Starlink's satellite beams were "turned off over India" and were "never on in the first place", a remark he repeated on Wednesday.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS Wall Street en repli, les rendements obligataires pèsent
item.description: La Bourse de New York a fini en baisse mercredi, au lendemain de records du S&P-500 et du Nasdaq, alors que les rendements des bons du Trésor américain à échéance longue ont repris leur progression et ravivé les craintes des investisseurs à propos de l'inflation et de l'ampleur de la dette.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: La Bourse de New York a fini en baisse mercredi, au lendemain de records du S&P-500 et du Nasdaq, alors que les rendements des bons du Trésor américain à échéance longue ont repris leur progression et ravivé les craintes des investisseurs à propos de l'inflation et de l'ampleur de la dette. L'indice Dow Jones (.DJI) a cédé 0,66%, ou 341,11 points, à 51.180,17 points. Le S&P-500 (.SPX) , plus large, a perdu 17,18 points, soit 0,22%, à 7.801,75 points. Le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) a reculé de son côté de 61,19 points (0,22%) à 27.538,69 points. Le Nasdaq finit dans le rouge pour la première fois en six séances, tandis que le S&P-500 et le Nasdaq voient leur série de quatre séances dans le vert s'arrêter. Après avoir reculé mardi, les prix du pétrole ont rebondi, le Brent ayant brièvement dépassé le seuil des 100 dollars le baril. Parallèlement, le rendement des bons du Trésor américain à 30 ans s'est établi à un pic de 24 ans. Dans un contexte de guerre prolongée entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran, les préoccupations sur l'approvisionnement en pétrole ont provoqué une flambée des prix énergétiques, ce qui alimente les craintes à propos de pressions inflationnistes plus larges et par conséquent d'un cycle durable de resserrement monétaire. En y ajoutant les niveaux élevés de la dette des entreprises et de la dette publique américaine, la situation a provoqué ces dernières semaines des secousses sur les marchés financiers. Les investisseurs espéraient "un peu de répit avec le pétrole, qui aurait permis un peu de répit avec les taux et aurait donc aidé le marché boursier", a commenté Thomas Martin, gestionnaire de portfolio chez GLOBALT, à Atlanta. Notant que "le troisième trimestre était supposé être le plus faible de l'année" avec pour effet une correction sur les marchés, mais que cela ne s'était "pas produit", il a déclaré que les investisseurs en profitaient pour prendre des bénéfices. Les principaux indices de Wall Street ont effacé en fin de séance une partie de leurs pertes initiales après que l'Agence internationale de l'énergie (AIE) a annoncé vouloir accélérer la libération de réserves de pétrole, en priorité de diesel, ce qui a provoqué une baisse des prix du brut. Par ailleurs, le compte-rendu de la réunion de septembre de la Réserve fédérale (Fed), publié dans l'après-midi, montre des divisions parmi les responsables de la banque centrale américaine à propos de la logique justifiant de relever les taux, bien qu'a été décidée à l'unanimité la hausse du coût de l'emprunt opérée le mois dernier. Certains participants ont dit voir une hausse des taux comme nécessaire pour se prémunir des répercussions du choc énergétique, tandis que d'autres ont souligné vouloir lutter contre l'inflation alimentée par la solidité de la demande. D'après des données FedWatch de CME, les marchés financiers misent actuellement à environ 17% à peine sur l'hypothèse d'une nouvelle baisse des taux lors de la réunion d'octobre de la Fed, contre plus de 37% une semaine plus tôt. "Il y a toujours l'anticipation de hausses des taux supplémentaires, mais pas forcément à chaque réunion, et c'est ce que dit le marché: octobre sera une pause", a déclaré Thomas Martin. A noter, mercredi, le secteur des semiconducteurs, parmi les catalyseurs de Wall Street cette année, a fini en baisse de 1,2%. Parmi les secteurs majeurs du S&P-500, les soins de santé (.SPXHC) ont enregistré les gains les plus importants. A l'inverse, l'industrie (.SPLRCI) a subi la plus forte baisse. SpaceX (SPCX.O) a cédé 2,5% après des informations de presse selon lesquelles le groupe détenu par Elon Musk désirait obtenir 40 milliards de dollars de financements en vue de l'acquisition de puces de Nvidia.
